question: Can the Electron Main boundary (private app protocol, strict CSP, sender/frame IPC validation, deny-by-default navigation/window/webview/download/permission, release fuse verification) keep a compromised renderer from escaping, proven with real Electron fixtures?

proves: af-app protocol serves only real files inside the renderer asset root; traversal, encoded traversal, backslash, NUL, host spoofing and symlink escape return 403/404 with no secret leak and no network fallback (SV1-ELECTRON-01)

IPC is serviced only for the expected webContents top frame at the app origin; unexpected webContents, subframe, destroyed sender, navigated frame and foreign origin are denied; arbitrary channel names hit 'No handler registered' (SV1-ELECTRON-02/06)
navigation, window.open, target=_blank, webview attach, download and permission requests are all denied by default in a real Electron run (SV1-ELECTRON-03)
strict CSP blocks eval, Function constructor, external script/fetch and inline script while allowing 'self' assets (SV1-ELECTRON-04)

the dev Electron Framework binary carries fuse wire '10110001' (RunAsNode / NODE_OPTIONS / CLI-inspect enabled) and is flagged non-compliant by verifyReleaseFuses; behaviorally, the unfused binary honors ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE and NODE_OPTIONS --require injection, while an ad-hoc-resigned clone with the three injection fuses flipped off refuses both and still boots (SV1-ELECTRON-05)
a wrong-fuse or unparseable binary fails closed in release verification (SV1-T-16/SV1-T-21, wire level)
doesNotProve: OnlyLoadAppFromAsar / EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation behavior — needs a packaged, signed, notarized release build (SV1-SUPPLY-03); verified at wire level only
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS injection — no dedicated Electron fuse exists; mitigation path must be decided at distribution level
preload MessagePort / Attachment binding (second half of SV1-ELECTRON-06) — no streams exist in R0
IPC payload schema / size / rate limits and per-route capability (SV1-ELECTRON-02 tail) — Daemon-side, pending RuntimeLimitProfile freeze
SV1-ELECTRON-07 confirmation surfaces (Trust / destructive / Launch Confirmation) — separate slice
Daemon-side schema enforcement half of SV1-T-04 — covered by transport/contracts slices, not this one

traversal.note: literal '..' normalized by Chromium URL parser before the handler

fuses.devBinaryVerdict: non-compliant (RunAsNode, EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable, EnableNodeCliInspectArguments, GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges on; asar integrity off)

flippedFuseClone.resign: ad-hoc (codesign --force --sign -) on a throwaway tmp clone

fuses.syntheticWireRoundTrip: parse/flip/verify unit-tested; exactly REQUIRED_RELEASE_FUSES passes, any single deviation fails closed

reproduction: AF_PROBE_EVIDENCE=1 pnpm vitest run apps/desktop/src/__tests__/electron-boundary.test.ts  # dumps the raw fixture JSON as AF_EVIDENCE=...
notes: All fixture Electron apps and flipped binaries are throwaway artifacts under $TMPDIR; node_modules is only read, never modified.

The macOS fuse wire format (sentinel + version byte 1 + length byte 9 + ASCII flags in FuseKey order) was confirmed empirically against Electron 43.2.0 (9 fuses; index 8 = WasmTrapHandlers, added since 34.5.8).

Dev/release difference: dev loads the vite dev server over http://localhost (no af-app, no CSP); the IPC origin allowlist is bound to the actually loaded origin in both forms, tested via the devPosture probe.
